clue.text: French mediation service in uproar

parts.note: ACAS is the UK's Advisory, Conciliation and Arbitration Service, which mediates in workplace disputes

explanation.surface: A French conciliation body finds its talks collapsing into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: ACAS is a British public body that steps in to settle disputes between employers and unions.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracas is a noisy quarrel or brawl, the kind of disturbance an uproar describes.

clue.text: Truth about column brought about improvement to features

indicators.note: about means going round, so the truth surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a fact is a truth

indicators.note: brought about means turned round, so the word for column is reversed

parts.note: a file is a column of people one behind another

explanation.surface: A truthful newspaper column led to better facial features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' looks like journalism; it is a file, a line of people walking one behind another, which 'brought about' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is cosmetic surgery that tightens the skin to make the face look younger.

clue.text: Monarch upset mainly with TV presenter

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of Monarch are put into a new order
mainly means most of it, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: and means with, together

explanation.surface: An upset monarch mostly sides with a television host.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorman is the main presenter of a news broadcast who links the reports.

clue.text: Political alliance is supporting 50% cuts

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the word is placed below the other piece
50% means only half of the word for cuts is kept

parts.note: axes are cuts, as in budget cuts

explanation.surface: A political pact backs cutting spending in half.
explanation.walkthrough: The Axis was the alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is a pact between powers, most famously the wartime Berlin-Rome-Tokyo bloc.

clue.text: What is made after changing law?

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of after are put into a different order

parts.note: an act is a law passed by a parliament

explanation.surface: A riddle about legislation: what results once a law has been amended?
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing law' reads as amending a statute, but 'changing' acts only on the word before it, and the law is an act of parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is an object made by human hands, a manufactured thing.

clue.text: Famous musician tips backing singer

parts.note: tips means tilts or rocks

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for singer is read backwards

parts.note: a rat is an informer, someone who sings to the police

explanation.surface: A star offers advice to a backing vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing singer' looks like a backup vocalist; 'singer' is an informer, a RAT, and 'backing' reverses it to TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock star is a celebrated performer of rock music.

clue.text: Stable states question India and African country promoting English

indicators.note: promoting means moving up, so the letter for English is shifted to the front

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Liberia is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Questions about the stability of India and a West African state.
explanation.walkthrough: QU, I and LIBERIA run together; 'promoting' lifts the E out of LIBERIA to the front, leaving LIBRIA at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Equilibria is the plural of equilibrium, a balanced condition in which forces cancel out.

clue.text: The best record covered by Norwegian band

indicators.note: covered by means enclosed within, so the record goes inside the band

parts.note: a-ha is the Norwegian pop group known for Take On Me
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A top hit covered by a Norwegian pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered' suggests a cover version; here it means wrapped inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha, the first Greek letter, denotes the top or dominant one, as in an alpha male.

clue.text: Fool was among the first with a peerage?

parts.note: tit is British slang for a fool
led means was in front, among the leaders

explanation.surface: A dig at a foolish early recipient of an aristocratic rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding a peerage bears a title such as lord or earl, so is titled.

clue.text: Confused like all ratings most of the time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bewildered, at a loss

definitions.text: like all ratings most of the time
definitions.meaning: second meaning: on a voyage, as naval ratings usually are

explanation.walkthrough: 'ratings' suggests scores or viewing figures; in the navy ratings are ordinary sailors, who spend much of their service afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both puzzled and out on the ocean aboard a ship.

clue.text: Commuter who's trapped on the Circle Line?

definitions.text: Commuter who's trapped on the Circle Line?

parts.words: Commuter who's trapped on the Circle Line?
parts.note: the Circle Line is a London Underground loop, but here the circle is a wheel: this commuter rides on wheels

explanation.walkthrough: London's Circle Line is a looping Tube line where a passenger might seem stuck going round; read 'circle' as a wheel and the commuter is pedalling to work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bike rider goes everywhere perched on a pair of circular wheels, so the cryptic picture fits someone pedalling to work.

clue.text: Women in warped view of true male chauvinist pig?

definitions.text: Women in warped view of true male chauvinist pig?

indicators.note: warped means bent out of shape, so the letters of true and MCP are twisted into a new order

parts.note: MCP is the common abbreviation for male chauvinist pig

explanation.surface: A sideswipe at a sexist man's distorted way of seeing women.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: crumpet is British slang for women seen as sex objects, exactly the warped view of such a man.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang crumpet means women regarded purely as objects of sexual desire, a sexist usage.

clue.text: Money can corrupt in the end

parts.note: can is slang for toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of corrupt

explanation.surface: A cynic's maxim that cash will always corrupt people eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: both can and loo are British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is informal slang for cash, as well as for stolen goods.

clue.text: Some syndicates sell at exhibitions to come together as one

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Business groups market their wares at trade shows to pool their efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapes that tessellate fit together without gaps to form one continuous pattern.

clue.text: What manipulates body and frame of any set photo spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so those letters with set photo are rearranged
frame of means the outside letters, first and last, of any

explanation.surface: Instructions for arranging a set of photographs within a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopathy is a therapy that treats ailments by massaging and moving the bones and muscles.

clue.text: Withhold food from female religious community

parts.note: the Amish are a Christian community in the US known for plain living

explanation.surface: A woman in a strict religious group is denied food.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is an old verb meaning to starve someone, depriving them of nourishment.

clue.text: Writers following on from author's verse

parts.note: the author is, in the first person, is I am
Bics are ballpoint pens, named after the brand

explanation.surface: Writers carry on in the wake of an author's poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'author' or 'setter' is often the speaker, I; 'author's' expands as 'author is', so I AM. 'following on from' puts BICS after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambics is poetry written in iambs, metrical feet of an unstressed then a stressed syllable.

clue.text: Enrich broadcast over IP with good encryption

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so Enrich and IP are mixed up

explanation.surface: Tech jargon about boosting a transmission over internet protocol with sound coding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciphering means putting a message into code, which is what encryption does.

clue.text: Captures "nearness" in a different way

indicators.note: in a different way says the letters of nearness are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Something grasps the idea of closeness from a new angle.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnare is to trap or catch, as in a snare.

clue.text: Form of Buddhism stifling very quiet priest's craft

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the outer word holds the others inside

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A meditative religion silencing a holy man's skills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill; it means an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A zeppelin is a rigid airship, a kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Broadcaster's back-to-back articles about X

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking definition and wordplay

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles go round the other piece

parts.note: the article an placed next to its own mirror image, na, gives anna
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a broadcaster and the mysterious X.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-back' means an article followed by its own reflection; 'X' is not a mark or an unknown but the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: An antenna is an aerial, the device that transmits radio and television signals.

clue.text: Wife replaces front of plain veil

indicators.note: replaces front of means the first letter of the word for plain is swapped out for the new piece

parts.note: plain means simple, unadorned

explanation.surface: A wife swaps a simple veil for something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimple is a cloth headdress covering head and neck, worn by medieval women and some nuns.

clue.text: Rebuke woman embracing Queen?

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the woman surrounds the queen

parts.note: she refers to a woman
a queen is a female cat

explanation.surface: A woman scolds while hugging the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' with its question mark is not royalty but a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To scathe is an archaic verb meaning to criticise harshly, as in scathing.

clue.text: Ethical person for example in position of leadership

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the leading position

explanation.surface: A principled person serves as a model in a leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegan avoids all animal products, usually on moral grounds.

clue.text: Primate greeting politician hosted by Canadian/US character

indicators.note: hosted by means held inside, so the greeting and politician sit within the outer letters

parts.note: CAN is the abbreviation for Canadian
hi is a greeting
MP is a Member of Parliament
zee is the American name for the letter Z

explanation.surface: A primate is welcomed by a politician, guest of a North American figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosted by' places the greeting and politician just after the first letter of the host pair. Americans say 'zee' for the last letter of the alphabet, where Britons and Canadians say 'zed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimpanzee is an African great ape, one of the primates closest to humans.

clue.text: Lives disrupted by incomplete treatment plans

indicators.note: disrupted by means broken apart by the other piece inserted in it

parts.note: is means exists or lives

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a deal is treatment, as in a raw deal

explanation.surface: Lives are thrown off course by unfinished medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' suggests medicine; it is a deal, the way one is treated, and 'incomplete' drops the end to give DEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas can mean intentions or schemes, as in having ideas of moving abroad.

clue.text: Ultimately, slimy algae will envelop bay

indicators.note: Ultimately points to the final letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A warning that slimy algae will swamp a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks like the coastal inlet; it is the verb, a dog's howl.
explanation.definitionFit: To bay is to howl like a hound, and a yelp is a short sharp cry of a dog.

clue.text: Alternative Vote supported by rising star

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters are read upwards, reversed

parts.note: AV is the abbreviation for the Alternative Vote electoral system
on means resting upon, so A on B is A supported by B

explanation.surface: A reformed voting system gets backing from a politician on the up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares to great brightness before fading.

clue.text: Speaker who used social media

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small loudspeaker for high-pitched sounds
second meaning: someone who posted on Twitter

explanation.walkthrough: The 'Speaker' seems to be a person addressing an audience; it is hi-fi equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is both a hi-fi unit for treble notes and a person posting short messages on Twitter.

clue.text: Adult party unlikely to welcome guests?

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a social is an informal party or gathering

explanation.surface: A grown-up party that oddly seems set to turn guests away.
explanation.definitionFit: An asocial person avoids company and has no interest in mixing with others, so would hardly invite visitors.

clue.text: Barnes, say, is this to some extent

definitions.text: Barnes, say, is this to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says only part of the preceding words is used, a run of letters hidden within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A literary remark that the novelist Julian Barnes is partly an essay writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'extent' as the definition, but it cannot mean the answer and 'to some extent' is the hiding signal; the whole clue defines, with Julian Barnes as the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Barnes, the English novelist, has also published collections of essays, so he is an example of an essay writer.

clue.text: Create discord with half-hearted idiot's gibberish

parts.note: to jar is to clash or grate, creating discord

indicators.note: half-hearted means losing half of the centre, one of the two middle letters

parts.note: a goon is a fool; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A fool's nonsense stirs up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is specialist language that sounds like meaningless babble to outsiders.
